clips.send: Food, water, space, shelter, disease, predators, and weather can all limit population growth. Carrying capacity (K) is the largest population a habitat can support over time under a given set of conditions. Change one condition and see how the curve changes. More rabbits can give foxes enough food to survive and raise more young, so fox numbers may rise after a delay. More hunting can then reduce rabbit numbers, and fox numbers may fall as prey gets scarce. This feedback illustrates ecosystem self-regulation. The model treats rabbits as the foxes’ only prey. Depending on the settings, the curves can rise and fall repeatedly or level off. Drought can also change the pattern.
